questions.prompt: Two places are 30° of longitude apart. How far apart are their local times?
hints: The Earth turns 360° in 24 hours, so 15° every hour.
That makes 4 minutes of time for each degree.
solution: Each degree of longitude is 4 minutes of time.
30 × 4 = 120 minutes = 2 hours.

questions.prompt: When it is 12:00 at Greenwich (0°), what is the local time at 45°E?
hints: The Sun rises in the east, so places to the east reach noon first.
East of you: add time. West of you: take time away.
solution: 45° × 4 minutes = 3 hours.
45°E is east of Greenwich, so add 3 hours: 15:00.

longitude_and_time.title: Four minutes for every degree
longitude_and_time.big_idea: The Earth turns a full 360° in 24 hours. That is 15° every hour, or 4 minutes for every degree of longitude. A common slip is to use 15 minutes per degree, which makes every answer far too big.
steps: Find how many degrees of longitude apart the places are.
Turn the minutes into hours and minutes.
Check: 15° should always come out as exactly 1 hour.
longitude_and_time.sense_check: India spans about 30° of longitude, so the Sun rises about 2 hours earlier in Arunachal Pradesh than in Gujarat, not 7½ hours.

worked_examples.prompt: Two places are 30° of longitude apart. How far apart are their local times?

east_west_time.title: East is ahead, west is behind
east_west_time.big_idea: The Sun rises in the east, so places to the east of Greenwich have reached later in the day. Going east you add time; going west you take time away.
steps: Work out the time difference (4 minutes per degree).
Is the place east (E) or west (W) of Greenwich?
East: add the difference. West: subtract it.
India (82°30′E) is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of Greenwich.
east_west_time.sense_check: When it is noon in London, offices in India are already open for the afternoon.
